source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
With the raised platform blending into the overall design and the proportions coming together, this is really beginning to feel like a real machine. Everything looks great so far.

As the layout is refined, I have a few questions:

• Once finalized, what will the cup-clearance height be beneath the spouts? I want to ensure standard cups fit comfortably during pours.

• What route will the tubing and drain path take from the bowls to the spouts, and how concealed and serviceable will that system be?

• Given the current tower spacing and motor placement, will the bowls remain easy to remove for cleaning?

• If the motors or electronics ever require adjustment or replacement, how accessible will they be for maintenance?

I’m very happy with the direction overall and excited to see the next phase come together.

value_updates.maintenance_access: The tubing and drain system must remain serviceable, and motors and electronics must be accessible for maintenance, adjustment, and replacement.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Regarding clearance beneath the spouts, I’ll verify it tomorrow morning. The provisional estimate is about 7 inches, perhaps 7.25. The drain path from the bowls to the spouts will normally be completely hidden; it becomes somewhat visible when a bowl is removed, then is concealed again once a new bowl is installed.

Serviceability will be straightforward throughout the system. Both the top and bottom panels can be removed to access the machine, and the motor towers can be opened when the motors themselves need servicing. The bowls will still be easy to remove.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports that the removable top and bottom panels provide internal access and that the motor towers can be opened for motor servicing.
